Credential chip

.dr-chip · --claim · --sm · .dr-chips · --stack · components/badge.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

Verified by DRONInsured
  1. 1.dr-chipsThe row that holds credentials: wraps, gap 6. On the operator card it also wears .dr-op__badges, which adds a 9px top margin.
  2. 2.dr-chipThe pill: radius 999, padding 5 / 10, 12/600 caption type, gap 6. 26.8 high; measured 164.1 wide for Verified by DRON.
  3. 3.dr-ic:first-childThe leading mark, 14px. A shield with a check inside it on Verified by DRON; a plain shield on Insured.
  4. 4.dr-ic:last-childThe trailing tick, 14px. It says confirmed rather than merely stated, so the chip is never reduced to its colour.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Verification badge.

When to use

The credential chip answers RJ-C1, the highest single drop-off in the CJM: confirm the operator is real and qualified. So the credentials sit on the operator card, beside the name and job count and before any tap, never on a profile page behind a click. Claim chips stand on the six tracking* files, the four order-confirmed* files, account (Verified with Diia), operator-account (Insured, CAA licence) and inspection-report (Verified by DRON on the signature row). The same chip family also carries plain facts on review cards, job offers and reports, and, at --sm, the New mark and the availability badge.

The rule reads in one line: green means DRON confirmed this document, grey means a plain supporting fact. Green is the tint behind a charcoal label, never the letters, so the chip does not break the fill-only rule; it is the rule. The shield with a check, the plain shield and the trailing tick make the difference legible in drawing as well as in colour (WCAG 1.4.1). A --trust blue rung for third-party confirmation is declared in the ui/kit.css archive and drawn nowhere; it was not ported into components/.

The words are facts, not adjectives: Verified by DRON, Insured, CAA licence, Verified with Diia. On order-confirmed-empty alone the claim is shortened to Verified so the pair fits one row.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Chips and badges · § Named rules (One Accent) · inventory.md § 1 (Verification badge) · microcopy.md § order-confirmed, tracking · voice.md P2

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Andriy M. 4.9 ★ · 214 jobs Verified by DRONInsured

Credentials on the card, under the name they vouch for, readable without a tap. This is the operator card on tracking.

Don’t

Book again

A chip used as a control. A chip states a fact and takes no tap; an action is a button, and an applied filter that can be removed is the filter chip of in-page tabs. A state that changes, such as availability, is the availability badge.
